research_rationale: EO 11031 (June 19, 1962) extended the committee for four years ending June 30, 1966 (sec. 1), re-appointed its three appointive members for a four-year period ending the same day (sec. 2(a)), continued the two designated members at the Secretaries' pleasure (sec. 2(b)) and amended EO 6783 accordingly (sec. 3). The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. Secs. 1 and 2(a) ended by their own terms on June 30, 1966; secs. 2(b) and 3 had no term of their own and ceased with the committee that day. The draft's EVENT_BEFORE_SIGNING conflicts came from a catalog note listing earlier extensions (EOs 10134, 10541, 10589, 10767) that predate and do not affect this order. Whole-order end: 1966-06-30.

research_rationale: EO 8688 (February 19, 1941), under the act of October 17, 1940 (Public No. 872, 76th Congress), prescribed regulations for quarters allowances to Army enlisted men of the first three grades with dependents: definitions of dependent and children (para. 1) and the entitlement, effective as of October 17, 1940, measured by the non-travel quarters rates of EO 7293 'or any amendments thereto, issued under section 11' of the 1922 act, plus a lodging allowance for Philippine Scouts (para. 2). EO 9206 (7 FR 5851), signed July 27, 1942 under section 10 of the act of June 16, 1942 (Public Law 607, 77th Congress), prescribed new allowance regulations and in its closing paragraph superseded EO 8688, EO 8704 'as amended by Executive Order No. 8759' and EO 9105, and 'shall be effective as of June 1, 1942'. First_end uses that stated effective date, not the signing date. No earlier event ending any of these provisions was found: the OFR catalog notes record only the amendments by EOs 8759 and 9105 and the supersession by EO 9206. Catalog notes were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). The rate cross-reference in para. 2a is read as reaching the rates of EO 8704, which replaced EO 7293's rates under the same section 11; on either reading the entitlement itself continued until the supersession. EO 9206's section on enlisted men of the first three grades with dependents re-enacted the substance under the 1942 act. Every clause ended on 1942-06-01; whole-order end 1942-06-01.

research_rationale: EO 8704 (March 4, 1941), under section 11 of the act of June 10, 1922, prescribed the allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey and Public Health Service not furnished quarters or rations in kind: Table I (station allowances) with two notes, Table II (travel allowances) with four notes, and a closing paragraph superseding EO 7293 and its amendments, effective on the date of the order except for continental quarters allowances (July 1, 1941). EO 8759 (May 24, 1941) added Exception No. 5 to Table I and EO 9105 (March 19, 1942) inserted a paragraph on advance payments; both are recorded as later events, not ends. EO 9206 (7 FR 5851), signed July 27, 1942 under section 10 of the act of June 16, 1942 (Public Law 607, 77th Congress), prescribed new allowance regulations and in its closing paragraph superseded EO 8688, EO 8704 'as amended by Executive Order No. 8759' and EO 9105, and 'shall be effective as of June 1, 1942'. First_end uses that stated effective date, not the signing date. No earlier event ending any of these provisions was found: the OFR catalog notes record only the amendments by EOs 8759 and 9105 and the supersession by EO 9206. Catalog notes were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). The tables, notes and regulations ended on 1942-06-01. The closing supersession and deferred-effective-date provisions were one-time and complete on July 1, 1941. The text layer of this page interleaves columns; each clause quotes the verbatim fragments as printed (see text_note) and the clause inventory follows the printed structure. Whole-order end 1942-06-01.

By virtue of the authority vested in me  
by section 11 of the act of June 10, 1922,  
c. 212, 42 Stat. 625, 630, as amended by  
the act of November 21, 1941 (Public  
Law 319, 77th Congress), Executive Or­
der No. 8704 of March 4, 1941, as  
amended by Executive Order No. 8759  
of May 24, 1941, prescribing regulations  
governing the granting of allowances  
for quarters and subsistence to enlisted  
men of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps,  
Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Sur­
vey, and Public Health Service who are  
not furnished quarters or rations in  
kind, is hereby further amended by in­
serting, before the last paragraph  
thereof, a new paragraph, reading as  
follows:
“Payments of allowances for quarters 
and subsistence may be made to enlisted  
men not more than one month in ad­
vance, except that as to men proceeding  
to or from a station beyond the conti­
nental limits of the United States or in  
Alaska, such payments may be made  
not more than three months in advance.  
The heads of the Departments concerned  
may prescribe such additional regula­
tions as may be necessary to carry out  
the provisions of this paragraph.”

research_rationale: EO 11641 (January 28, 1972) had the Attorney General establish an Office for Drug Abuse Law Enforcement in the Department of Justice (sec. 1(a)), headed by a Director with the title Special Assistant Attorney General (sec. 1(b)) who also served as Special Consultant to the President (sec. 1(c)) and ran a concentrated federal enforcement program (sec. 1(d)); required consultation with the Special Action Office for Drug Abuse Prevention (sec. 2); placed the Director in level IV by amending EO 11248 sec. 1 (sec. 3); and required agency assistance (sec. 4). EO 11727 of July 6, 1973 (38 FR 18357) recites that Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1973, effective July 1, 1973, establishes the Drug Enforcement Administration into which both offices' functions would be merged; it revokes EO 11641 (sec. 2) and EO 11676 (sec. 3), directs the Attorney General to reassign their functions, abolish the offices and wind up their affairs (secs. 2, 3, 5), deletes both directors from level IV as listed in EO 11708 (sec. 4), and is 'effective as of July 1, 1973' (sec. 6). First_end uses that stated effective date, not the July 6 signing date. One earlier partial end (also noted by the OFR catalog, which records EO 11248 as revoked by EO 11708): sec. 3 of this order had inserted its director into EO 11248 sec. 1, and EO 11708 sec. 3 (March 23, 1973) revoked EO 11248 as amended except for level V positions, so sec. 3 ended on 1973-03-23 (EO 11708 sec. 1 placed the director anew, and EO 11727 sec. 4 later deleted that placement). The U.S. Code note under 21 U.S.C. 801 (release point 119-121), which reprints EO 11727, and the eCFR hits were read: they record the revocation and nothing continuing. The 1989 Codification disposition table and the OFR catalog note were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). Whole-order end 1973-07-01.

research_rationale: EO 9958 (May 15, 1948), under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, created a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between National Airlines, Inc. and employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, directed it to report within thirty days, and restated the statutory status quo. EO 9965 of June 3, 1948 (13 FR 3009) created a board, naming its three members, for the disputes between the carrier and employees represented by both the pilots' association and the International Association of Machinists, and expressly superseded EO 9958; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. The supersession came within this order's thirty-day reporting period; no earlier report or other end is recorded in the held sources, and none is inferred from the deadline. The 1989 Codification disposition table and the OFR catalog note were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison).
